prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1122; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claimant reference you have.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on the main road in Pearland, in the right lane near the shopping center.
Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. The other car hit me pretty hard.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?
A: No. I was looking at the light, and I didn't have time to react.
Q: Did you get out of your car and speak with the other driver?
A: The other driver came over and apologized. She said she had looked down at her phone for a second.
Q: How are you feeling now?
A: Not great. I have a constant headache, I feel dizzy when I move quickly, and bright lights bother my eyes. I also have trouble concentrating at work.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since the accident?
A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic that same day, and they told me it could be a concussion. I've been referred to a neurologist and I'm waiting on that appointment.
Q: Are you currently taking any medication for the symptoms?
A: Over-the-counter pain relievers only. My doctor asked me to avoid screens for long periods and to rest as much as possible.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm worried about how long my recovery will take, and I'd like to understand what coverage is available for my medical care and lost time from work.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you about those questions shortly.
A: Thank you.
